entries.name: Ainu
entries.definition: A critically endangered language of the Ainu people of northern Japan.

entries.name: Akan
entries.definition: A language spoken mainly in Ghana, with varieties such as Twi and Fante.

entries.name: Algebraic Logic Functional
entries.definition: A programming language that combines functional and logic programming.

entries.name: American Sign Language
entries.definition: A sign language used mainly by Deaf communities in the United States and English-speaking Canada.

entries.name: AMPscript
entries.definition: Salesforce Marketing Cloud's scripting language for personalizing the content of emails, landing pages and other messages.

entries.name: ArchiMate
entries.definition: An open modelling language, maintained by The Open Group, for describing enterprise architecture across business, application and technology layers.

entries.name: ASP.NET Razor
entries.definition: A markup syntax from Microsoft for embedding C# or Visual Basic code in HTML to generate web pages on the server.

entries.name: Aymara
entries.definition: An indigenous language of the Andes spoken mainly in Bolivia, Peru and Chile.

entries.name: Base SAS
entries.definition: The core of the SAS system, providing the SAS programming language with its DATA step, procedures and macro facility for data management and analysis.

entries.name: Bassa
entries.definition: A Kru language of Liberia spoken by the Bassa people, not to be confused with the Bantu language Basaa of Cameroon.

entries.name: Batak
entries.definition: A group of related Austronesian languages spoken by the Batak peoples of northern Sumatra, Indonesia.

entries.name: Bemba
entries.definition: A Bantu language spoken mainly in northern Zambia and nearby parts of the Democratic Republic of the Congo.

entries.name: Benga
entries.definition: A Bantu language spoken along the coast of Equatorial Guinea and Gabon.

entries.name: Bengali
entries.definition: An Indo-Aryan language spoken mainly in Bangladesh and the Indian state of West Bengal.

entries.name: Berber
entries.definition: A family of related Afro-Asiatic languages spoken across North Africa, also known as the Amazigh languages.

entries.name: C++
entries.definition: Writing programs in C++.

entries.name: Carib
entries.definition: A Cariban language spoken by the Kalina (Kari'nja) people along the coasts of northern South America.

entries.name: Castilian Spanish
entries.definition: The standard variety of the Spanish language as spoken in Spain, especially in its central and northern regions.

entries.name: Catalan
entries.definition: A Romance language spoken mainly in Catalonia, the Balearic Islands, Valencia and Andorra, where it is the official language.

entries.name: Chakma
entries.definition: An Indo-Aryan language spoken by the Chakma people in Bangladesh and India.

entries.name: Chamorro
entries.definition: An Austronesian language spoken by the Chamorro people of Guam and the Northern Mariana Islands.

entries.name: Chinese
entries.definition: A group of related Sinitic languages, including Mandarin and Cantonese, spoken mainly in China and written in Chinese characters.

entries.name: Chipmunk Basic
entries.definition: A free BASIC interpreter for several platforms, based on classic Microsoft-style BASIC.

entries.name: COMIT
entries.definition: An early string-processing programming language developed at MIT in the 1950s for linguistic research and machine translation.

entries.name: C#
entries.definition: The C# programming language.

entries.name: CSS
entries.definition: Styling web documents with cascading style sheets.

entries.name: Czech
entries.definition: A West Slavic language spoken mainly in the Czech Republic.

entries.name: Dari
entries.definition: The variety of Persian that is an official language of Afghanistan.

entries.name: Dart
entries.definition: A programming language developed by Google, used mainly with the Flutter framework to build apps for several platforms.

entries.name: Dhivehi
entries.definition: The Indo-Aryan language of the Maldives, written in the Thaana script.

entries.name: Dinka
entries.definition: A Nilotic language spoken by the Dinka people of South Sudan.

entries.name: Duala
entries.definition: A Bantu language spoken in and around the city of Douala in Cameroon.

entries.name: ECMAScript 2015
entries.definition: The 2015 edition of the ECMAScript standard on which JavaScript is based, which added classes, modules, arrow functions and promises.

entries.name: Elixir
entries.definition: A dynamic, functional programming language that runs on the Erlang virtual machine.

entries.name: English
entries.definition: The English human language; not a programming language.

entries.name: Ewondo
entries.definition: A Bantu language spoken by the Beti people of central Cameroon, around Yaoundé.

entries.name: F#
entries.definition: A functional-first programming language for the .NET platform, developed at Microsoft Research.

entries.name: Fali
entries.definition: A group of related languages spoken by the Fali people of northern Cameroon.

entries.name: Forth
entries.definition: A stack-based, extensible programming language created by Charles H. Moore.

entries.name: French
entries.definition: A Romance language spoken in France and many other countries.
